terms.gloss: go without food, for a meal or longer
terms.grammar: abstineō with the ablative; also sē cibō abstinēre
evidence: Sen. Ep. 78.11: carēre adsuētīs voluptātibus, abstinēre cibō, sitīre, ēsurīre
terms.comment: To leave out one meal, say it plainly: hodiē nōn prandī, I skipped lunch today. One who has missed a meal is imprānsus or incēnātus (see “without lunch”, “without dinner”).

phrases.latin: Sed molestum est, inquit, carēre adsuētīs voluptātibus, abstinēre cibō, sitīre, ēsurīre.
phrases.english: “But it is hard,” he says, “to do without the pleasures you are used to, to go without food, to be thirsty, to be hungry.”
I skipped lunch today; that’s why I’m hungry.

sources: Lewis & Short: abstineo · Lewis & Short: cibus
